products.description: Fenugreek seeds are small, hard, yellow-amber colored kernels known for their powerful, bittersweet flavor and distinctive maple-syrup-like aroma. A staple in Indian, Middle Eastern, and North African cuisines, they are used both whole and ground as a spice to add depth to curries, pickles.

Sesame seeds (Sesamum indicum) are small, flat, oval seeds found in a variety of colorsâ€”from creamy white to jet black. Known for their mild, slightly nutty flavor and satisfying crunch, they are one of the world's oldest cultivated oilseed crops.

Cumin seeds (Cuminum cyminum) are small, elongated, brown seeds with characteristic ridges, recognizable for their intense, pungent, and earthy aroma. They are one of the most widely used spices globally, forming the flavor base for countless dishes across Indian, Mexican, Middle Eastern.

Chia seeds (Salvia hispanica) are tiny, black and white seeds native to Central and Southern Mexico, prized by ancient Aztec warriors for energy and endurance. Now famous as a modern "superfood," they are celebrated for their impressive nutritional profile, being extremely rich in Omega-3 fatty acid

Flax seeds (Linum usitatissimum), also known as linseeds, are small, glossy, brown or golden seeds famous for their exceptional health benefits. They are the richest plant source of the essential omega-3 fatty acid, Alpha-Linolenic Acid (ALA), crucial for heart health and reducing inflammation.

Castor seeds (often incorrectly called castor beans) are the mottled, oval seeds of the Ricinus communis plant. They are not used in cooking.The seed is primarily processed to extract Castor Oil, which is valued for its high concentration of ricinoleic acid.

Green Gram (Vigna radiata), commonly known as Moong or Mung Bean, is a small, olive-green legume highly valued across Asia. These tiny pulses are celebrated for being exceptionally easy to digest, making them a staple in health-focused diets and Ayurvedic tradition.

Fennel seeds (Foeniculum vulgare) are the dried, small, light green to tan-colored fruits of the fennel plant. They are instantly recognizable by their powerful, sweet aroma and distinctive anise/licorice-like flavor, caused by the compound anethole.
Mustard seeds are tiny,bold,round seeds that come in black colour. They are one of the oldest spices known, prized for their ability to add a sharp, pungent bite to food.
Mustard seeds are tiny,bold,round seeds that come in yellow colour. They are one of the oldest spices known, prized for their ability to add a sharp, pungent bite to food.
Red Cow Beans (Vigna unguiculata), also known as Red Lobia or Red Chori, are small, reddish-brown legumes with a characteristic nutty, earthy flavor and a tender texture when cooked.

Turmeric fingers are the dried, elongated rhizomes (underground stems) of the Curcuma longa plant, essentially the whole, unprocessed root of the spice we know as turmeric.Resembling gnarled fingers, they possess a rich, earthy, and slightly bitter flavor, and a deep orange-yellow color.

products.productName: BISHOPS SEEDS( Ajwain or Carom Seeds)
products.description: Bishop's Seeds (also known as Ajwain or Carom Seeds) are the tiny, light olive-green fruits of a herb related to parsley and cumin. They are immediately recognizable by their powerful, pungent, and slightly bitter flavor and aroma, which strongly resembles thyme.

Coriander seeds are the dried, globe-shaped fruits of the coriander plant, prized globally for their mild, warm, and highly aromatic flavor. Unlike the fresh leaves (cilantro), the seeds offer a delicate balance of citrus (orange peel), nutty, and slightly sweet notes.

Groundnut Dana is the edible, highly nutritious seed. It shares the nutritional and culinary profile of nuts, possessing a rich, creamy, and distinctively nutty flavor. Groundnuts are an extremely versatile and affordable food, being an best source of plant-based protein, healthy fats (oil).

Taramira seeds, also known as Arugula seeds or Jamba, are small, brown, oil-rich seeds popular in South Asia and West Asia. Known for being highly drought-resistant, they are primarily cultivated not for direct consumption, but for the extraction of their oil, known as Taramira Oil.

Desi Chickpeas often called Kala Chana (Black Chickpeas) or Bengal Gram, are the smaller, darker, and rougher-coated relative of the white Kabuli chickpea. They have a characteristically nutty, slightly earthy flavor and hold their shape well after cooking.

India, is the 9th largest subtropical Desert in the world. Deep beneath its glistening hot
sands, large pools of water form when the rare rains arrive during the monsoon season. As
the water seeps down, it combines with the mineral rich Desert Salt to form a thick saline
mixture. This is pumped up and left to dry in the Salt pans, creating dunes of one of the
purest forms of Desert Salt. Monsoon rains replenish the water levels each season creating
a sustainable cycle.
Why Lunn Desert Salt?
*Lunn is rich in  essential minerals like Zinc, Iodine, Potassium,
Magnesium, Calcium, Iron, Phosphorus & Sulphate for healthy living.
* Being a mild Salt, it enhances the natural flavour of your food.
Lunn is raw & pure. Suitable for daily cooking.
* Harvested from the Desert of Rajasthan, Lunn Salt is free from
microplastics.
* Salt forms lump naturally. An anti- caking agent keeps it free flowing.
Lunn Salt is free from this chemical additive.
What is Lunn?
* Lunn means â€˜Salt' in farmer's language.
* Being India's first Fair Trade certified Salt, Lunn ensure a fair price of
the Desert Salt to the farmers.
* Lunn Salt is 100% natural, hand harvested in an eco-friendly and
sustainable manner.

The brand LUNN was born when we noticed a need in common Salt which was
actually unhealthy. Salt is one of the only ingredients that cannot be skipped in any
meal. Even though it is such a necessity, we are not careful about the quality of Salt
we consume. In many researches and tests, microplastics have been found in Sea
Salt. The ocean being consumed by plastic not only disrupts and enters marine life
and organisms but also affects us since it is in the Salts being consumed. Other than
that, Table Salt and Common Salt are Salts that have been processed and refined to
such an extent that most of its mineral contents are lost. So Lunn has come with the
idea of producing organic & vegan salt, which is ethically & hand harvested in an
unpolluted Desert environment.

products.description: Psyllium Seeds are the dried seeds of the Plantago ovata plant, widely cultivated in India. Psyllium Husk is a natural soluble dietary fiber derived from the outer layer of Plantago ovata seeds, mainly cultivated in India. It is light cream in color, odorless, and tasteless, with excellent water-absorbing and swelling properties.

Psyllium Husk Powder is a finely ground, natural soluble dietary fiber obtained from the husk of Plantago ovata seeds, primarily grown in India. It is off-white in color, odorless, and tasteless, with excellent water absorption and swelling properties.

products.description: Cumin seeds are the dried seeds of the Cuminum cyminum plant, a member of the parsley family. They are widely used as a spice in cooking, especially in Indian, Middle Eastern, Latin American, and North African cuisines.
Fennel seeds are the dried seeds of the Foeniculum vulgare plant, a flavorful herb in the carrot family. They are commonly used as a spice and sometimes as a digestive aid.

Coriander refers to both the fresh leaves and the dried seeds of the Coriandrum sativum plant, which belongs to the parsley family. While the leaves are commonly known as cilantro, the seeds are used as a spice in various global cuisines.

Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is a herb widely used for its culinary, medicinal, and nutritional properties. It belongs to the Fabaceae (legume) family and is native to the Mediterranean region, southern Europe, and parts of Asia.

Dill seeds are the dried fruits of the dill plant (Anethum graveolens), an aromatic herb from the Apiaceae family, which also includes parsley, cumin, and coriander. Though the plant is mostly known for its feathery leaves (used as a fresh herb).

products.productName: Kalonji Seeds (Nigella Seeds) or black Cumin Seeds (Kala Jeera)
products.description: Kalonji (Nigella sativa), also known as black seed, black cumin, or Nigella, is a small black seed used as both a spice and a traditional remedy. It is widely used in Indian, Middle Eastern, and North African cuisines and traditional medicine systems such as Ayurveda and Unani.

Ajwain seeds (bishop Weed or Carom) are light to dark greenish brown in color. Ajwain seeds have a bitter and pungent taste with a characteristic odor and aroma. Its scientific name is TRACHYSPERMUM AMMI, from the Umbelliferae family.

Celery seeds are the small, dried fruits of the wild celery plant (Apium graveolens), a member of the Apiaceae family, which also includes carrots, parsley, and dill. Though tiny in size, celery seeds are intensely flavorful and widely used as a spice and in traditional medicine.

Chili whole refers to the dried whole fruits of chili peppers, typically from species like Capsicum annuum or Capsicum frutescens. These are widely used as a spice to add heat, color, and flavor to a variety of dishes in cuisines around the world, especially in Indian, Mexican, Thai, and Chinese.

Turmeric whole refers to the dried rhizome (underground stem) of the turmeric plant (Curcuma longa), a member of the ginger family (Zingiberaceae). It is widely used as a spice, natural dye, and traditional medicine, especially in Indian and Southeast Asian cultures.

Ginger (Zingiber officinale) is a flowering plant whose rhizome (underground stem) is widely used as a spice, flavoring agent, and medicinal root. It is native to South and Southeast Asia and has been cultivated for thousands of years for both culinary and therapeutic purposes.

Nutmeg is a warm, aromatic spice made from the seed of the nutmeg tree (Myristica fragrans), an evergreen native to the Spice Islands (Indonesia). It is valued for its sweet-spicy flavor and is used in both sweet and savory dishes around the world.

Cardamom is a highly aromatic spice made from the seeds of plants in the ginger family (Zingiberaceae), primarily Elettaria cardamomum (green cardamom) and Amomum species (black cardamom). It is known for its warm, sweet, and slightly citrusy flavor and is widely used in cooking, baking.

Cinnamon is a popular spice obtained from the inner bark of trees belonging to the genus Cinnamomum. It is prized for its warm, sweet, and woody flavor and has been used for thousands of years in cooking, baking, and traditional medicine.

Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is one of the most commonly used and historically significant spices in the world. It is derived from the dried fruit (peppercorns) of the black pepper vine, a flowering vine native to South India and Southeast Asia.

Psyllium seeds come from the plant Plantago ovata, a herbaceous annual native to parts of Asia and the Mediterranean. These tiny seeds are primarily valued for their high soluble fiber content and are commonly used to support digestive health.

Psyllium husk is the outer coating (husk) of the seeds of the psyllium plant (Plantago ovata). It is a highly soluble fiber known for its ability to absorb water and form a gel-like substance, making it a popular natural fiber supplement.

Basil (Ocimum basilicum) is an annual herb belonging to the mint family (Lamiaceae). Native to tropical regions from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, it has become a staple in global cuisines due to its distinct flavor and aroma.

Bay leaves are aromatic leaves from the bay laurel tree (Laurus nobilis), an evergreen shrub native to the Mediterranean region. These leaves are commonly used in cooking to impart a subtle, earthy flavor to various dishes. They are typically added whole during the cooking process.

Sesame seeds are small, oil-rich seeds that grow in pods on the Sesamum indicum plant, one of the oldest oilseed crops known to humanity. They have a mild, nutty flavor that becomes more pronounced when toasted. Hereâ€™s a breakdown of their characteristics

Groundnut, commonly known as peanut (Arachis hypogaea), is a leguminous plant belonging to the Fabaceae family. Despite its name, it is not a true nut but a legume, related to beans and lentils. Originating from South America, particularly the valleys of Paraguay.
Soybean (Glycine max) is a leguminous plant native to East Asia, renowned for its high protein content and versatility in various culinary and industrial applications.

Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa) is a highly nutritious, gluten-free pseudocereal native to the Andean region of South America. Often referred to as a â€œsuperfood,â€ quinoa has been cultivated for over 5,000 years and was a staple of ancient civilizations such as the Inca, Aymara, and Quechua people.

Chia seeds (Salvia hispanica) are tiny, nutrient-dense seeds from a flowering plant in the mint family, native to southern Mexico and Guatemala. Historically significant to Aztec and other Mesoamerican cultures, chia seeds were consumed for their energy-boosting properties.

Flaxseeds, also known as linseeds, are small, nutrient-dense seeds from the Linum usitatissimum plant. They have been cultivated for thousands of years, valued for both their fiber-rich seeds and strong fibers used in textiles. Today, flaxseeds are recognized for their numerous health benefits.

Makhana, also known as fox nuts or lotus seeds, are the edible seeds of the aquatic plant Euryale ferox, predominantly cultivated in regions like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh in India. These seeds are harvested from the flower of the plant, roasted to create a puffed, crunchy snack.

Dehydrated garlic is fresh garlic that has been dried to remove its moisture content, resulting in a shelf-stable product that retains much of its flavor and nutritional value. This process extends its shelf life and makes it convenient for storage and use.

Dehydrated Onion refers to onion that has been dried to remove most of its moisture content, preserving its flavor and extending its shelf life. It is commonly available in several forms, including flakes, granules, powder, and minced pieces.

products.description: A jewel in the Indian mithai tradition, Kaju Burfi is believed to have originated in North India. A sweet that began its journey in Karnatakaâ€™s royal kitchens, Mysore Pak is a true taste of tradition. Made with pure ghee, roasted Bengal gram flour, and sugar, this soft Mysore Pak from Sangam Sweets is a rich and flavorful Karnataka sweet loved by all.

A classic mithai made with slow-roasted gram flour, ghee, and sugar, Besan Laddu is a nostalgic favorite that never goes out of style. Its smooth, melt-in-the-mouth texture and warm aroma make it a comforting treat for celebrations, family gatherings.

Delicate, tiny boondi pearls soaked in syrup and bound with desi ghee, Motichur Laddu is a soft, premium treat loved across India. Crafted using time-honored techniques, this sweet is ideal for festive gifting, religious offerings, or simply enjoying with family.

products.description: Chilli powder is a spice made from ground dried chili peppers, used to add color, heat, and flavor to foods. It is created by drying and pulverizing the fruit of Capsicum plants, with the heat level varying based on the chili variety and measured on the Scoville scale
Turmeric powder is a bright yellow spice made from the dried and ground root of the Curcuma longa plant, a relative of ginger

Coriander powder, also called dhaniya powder, is a spice made by grinding the dried seeds of the coriander plant. It has a warm, earthy, and slightly citrusy flavor and aroma, and is a staple in many cuisines, particularly Indian cooking.
Cumin powder is a spice made from the dried, ground seeds of the Cuminum cyminum plant. It is a warm, earthy spice with a distinct nutty and slightly citrusy flavor.

videos.title: Samosa Manufacturing at Taj Frozen Foods , Nandur Unit
videos.description:
Spiral Freezing:
Concept: Spiral freezing is a method used to freeze food products quickly and uniformly. It involves placing the products on a conveyor belt that spirals up or down inside a freezing chamber.
Process:
1. Preparation:
o Food products (such as samosas) are placed on the conveyor belt.
2. Freezing:
o The conveyor belt moves the products through the freezing chamber.
o The chamber is maintained at very low temperatures using refrigerants.
o Cold air is circulated to ensure even freezing.
3. Advantages:
o Quick freezing helps maintain the quality and texture of the food.
o Efficient use of space due to the spiral design.
o Ideal for high-volume production.
Applications:
â€¢ Used in the food industry for freezing products like samosas, pastries, seafood, and prepared meals.
By combining traditional Punjabi samosa making with modern spiral freezing techniques, manufacturers can produce high-quality, frozen samosas that retain their taste and texture when reheated.

videos.title: Okra Processing at Taj Frozen Foods, Jejuri Unit
videos.description:
Frozen okra manufacturing typically involves a process known as Individually Quick Freezing (IQF). Hereâ€™s an overview of how frozen okra is manufactured and what IQF entails:
1. Harvesting and Sorting:
â€¢ Okra is harvested when it reaches the appropriate size and maturity.
â€¢ It undergoes initial sorting to remove damaged or low-quality pods.
2. Washing and Blanching:
â€¢ The okra pods are thoroughly washed to remove dirt and debris.
â€¢ Blanching follows, where the pods are briefly immersed in hot water or steam.
â€¢ Blanching helps to deactivate enzymes that can cause spoilage and preserves the color and texture of the okra.
3. Cooling:
â€¢ After blanching, the okra is rapidly cooled down to stop the cooking process and maintain freshness.
4. Individually Quick Freezing (IQF):
â€¢ IQF is a method of freezing where each individual piece of okra is frozen separately from the others.
â€¢ This is achieved by placing the okra on a conveyor belt or in a fluidized bed freezer.
â€¢ Quick freezing helps to preserve the natural flavor, color, and nutritional value of the okra.
â€¢ It also prevents the pieces from sticking together, allowing for easier portion control and thawing.
5. Packaging:
â€¢ Once frozen, the okra is typically packaged in bags or cartons suitable for freezer storage.
â€¢ Packaging is designed to protect the okra from freezer burn and contamination.
6. Storage and Distribution:
â€¢ Frozen okra is stored in cold storage facilities at temperatures below freezing to maintain quality.
â€¢ It is then distributed to retailers or food service providers for sale to consumers.
Benefits of IQF Process:
â€¢ Quality Preservation: IQF preserves the natural texture, flavor, and nutritional content of okra better than traditional freezing methods.
â€¢ Convenience: Each piece of okra freezes individually, allowing for easy portioning and use as needed.
â€¢ Long Shelf Life: Properly frozen and stored okra can maintain quality for an extended period.
Uses:
Frozen okra can be used in a variety of dishes such as soups, stews, curries, and as a side dish. Its convenience and retained quality make it a popular choice in both home cooking and commercial food preparation.
Overall, IQF technology plays a crucial role in ensuring that frozen okra retains its quality and nutritional value from farm to table.

products.description: Chilly powder is like the spicier version of salt in Indian culinary. Without it the food seems to be bland. And when have we Indians ever liked bland food?

products.description: Ajwain, also known as carom seeds or Bishop's weed (Trachyspermum ammi), are an aromatic Indian spice prized for their distinctive, pungent flavor and numerous traditional health benefits, particularly for digestion.

Bay leaves, primarily from the sweet bay tree (Laurus nobilis), are aromatic dried leaves widely used in cooking to infuse dishes with a subtle yet distinct herbal flavor and fragrance. They are typically removed before serving due to their tough, leathery texture.

Black pepper, derived from the dried, unripe fruit of the Piper nigrum vine, is one of the world's most traded and widely used spices. Known as the "King of Spices," it is celebrated globally for its pungent heat and sharp, aromatic flavor that enhances a vast array of culinary dishes

Black sesame seeds, harvested from the Sesamum indicum plant, are small, flat, oily seeds cherished globally for their distinctive nutty flavor, rich aroma, and high nutritional value. Black cardamom, often referred to as large cardamom or greater cardamom, is a potent and smoky spice derived from the dried pods of several species in the Amomum genus (Amomum subulatum being the most common).

Celery seeds are the dried, ripe fruits of the celery plant (Apium graveolens), used as a pungent and aromatic spice with a unique, earthy, and slightly bitter flavor. They are known for their strong, concentrated taste and numerous traditional medicinal uses.

Chickpeas, also widely known as garbanzo beans or chana (Cicer arietinum), are a highly valued annual legume celebrated globally for their nutty flavor, firm texture, and substantial nutritional benefits.

Crushed red chili, often labeled as crushed red pepper or chili flakes, is a popular condiment made from dried and crushed red chili peppers. It provides a versatile way to add a pungent heat and vibrant color to a wide array of savory dishes globally, from Italian to Indian cuisines.

Whole dried chilies are the mature, sun-dried fruit pods of various Capsicum plants, widely used globally to add a concentrated burst of heat, color, and complex flavor to dishes. The drying process intensifies their flavor,

Cumin seeds, known as jeera in India, are the dried, white fruit of the Cuminum cyminum plant. This ancient spice is highly valued globally for its warm, earthy flavor, distinctive aroma, and significant medicinal properties, especially as a powerful digestive aid.

Coriander powder, also known as ground coriander or dhaniya powder, is a popular spice made from the dried and ground seeds of the Coriandrum sativum plant. It provides a warm, earthy, and slightly citrusy flavor that is central to Indian and many other global cuisines.

Coriander seeds, known as dhaniya in India, are the dried, ripe fruits of the Coriandrum sativum plant. They are one of the world's oldest and most widely used spices, valued for their warm, nutty, and citrusy flavor that is distinct from the plant's fresh leaves (cilantro).

"Flat" cinnamon sticks are typically Cassia cinnamon (Cinnamomum cassia or similar species) which consists of a single, thick, and rough layer of bark. This contrasts with the more delicate, multi-layered quills of Ceylon ("true") cinnamon.

Cumin powder, also known as ground cumin or jeera powder, is a staple spice made by grinding the dried seeds of the Cuminum cyminum plant. It is widely used globally for its warm, earthy, and slightly bitter flavor, which adds depth and aroma to a variety of dishes.

Dried ginger, known as sonth or chukku in India, is made from fresh ginger rhizomes (Zingiber officinale) that have been carefully processed and dehydrated to remove their moisture content. This drying process concentrates its flavor and aroma, resulting in a spice with a sharp, pungent,

Fenugreek seeds, known as methi dana in Hindi, are the small, hard, yellowish-brown seeds of the annual herb Trigonella foenum-graecum. This robust spice is globally recognized for its distinct, slightly bitter taste.
